analysis_en.time: The study was conducted between November 2023 and February 2025 for the nursing home, and between December 2023 and December 2024 for the prison. The article was published on November 20, 2026 (N1, N46).
analysis_en.location_and_population: The study took place in an Italian nursing home and a remand prison. The nursing home housed 93 residents, with an average age of 86 years, and the prison accommodated approximately 75 individuals, with an average age of 47 years (N11, N15, N13).
analysis_en.event: An integrated monitoring system was developed and tested to assess respiratory infection risks in institutional settings, including human adenovirus as one of the viral targets. The system combined structural evaluations, indoor air and surface monitoring, wastewater testing, and clinical tracking (N1, N6).
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: The study identified operational contrasts between the two facilities, with the nursing home classified as low risk (structural score of 3) and the prison as high risk (structural score of 13). The nursing home population showed higher medical vulnerability, with 80% reporting previous pneumonia, while the prison population had higher lifestyle-related respiratory exposure (N12, N14, N16, N17).
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was a pilot project with limited clinical case counts and resource-intensive protocols. The researchers noted that simplified indicator panels require broader validation before routine adoption (N40).

news.title_zh: 综合监测系统绘制疗养院和监狱的呼吸道感染风险图 - Bioengineer.org
news.source_body_en: An integrated monitoring system was developed to assess respiratory infection risks in institutional settings, including nursing homes and prisons. The system combined structural evaluations, indoor air and surface monitoring, wastewater testing, and clinical tracking, as part of the Stell-ARI project by researchers from the University of Pisa and collaborating institutions. The study focused on two Italian facilities: a nursing home with 93 residents, mostly aged 86, and a remand prison housing approximately 75 individuals, mostly aged 47. The nursing home, constructed in 2022 and located in a low-traffic green area, had a low-risk structural score of 3 due to limited risk factors like the absence of dedicated air purifiers. In contrast, the prison, an older facility in an urban center, operated at 17% over capacity and had a high-risk structural score of 13, attributed to factors such as shared bathroom facilities and lack of automated temperature controls. The nursing home population showed higher medical vulnerability, with 80% reporting previous pneumonia, while the prison population had higher lifestyle-related respiratory exposure, including active smoking and substance abuse. The study highlighted the unique challenges of respiratory disease control in closed environments and emphasized the need for further validation of simplified monitoring methods before routine use.
news.content_zh: 开发了一个综合监测系统来评估疗养院和监狱等机构环境中的呼吸道感染风险。该系统结合了结构评估、室内空气和表面监测、废水测试和临床跟踪,是比萨大学和合作机构研究人员的 Stell-ARI 项目的一部分。该研究重点关注意大利的两处设施:一家拥有 93 名居民(大多年龄为 86 岁)的疗养院,以及一座容纳约 75 名居民(大多数年龄为 47 岁)的还押监狱。该疗养院建于 2022 年,位于人流量较少的绿地,由于缺乏专用空气净化器等有限的风险因素,其结构评分为 3 分低风险。相比之下,这座位于城市中心的较旧设施的监狱,由于共用浴室设施和缺乏自动温度控制等因素,其运营能力超额运行 17%,结构风险评分为 13 分。疗养院人口表现出更高的医疗脆弱性,其中 80% 的人曾患过肺炎,而监狱人口则有更高的与生活方式相关的呼吸道暴露,包括主动吸烟和药物滥用。该研究强调了封闭环境中呼吸系统疾病控制的独特挑战,并强调在常规使用之前需要进一步验证简化的监测方法。

news.content_title: Adenovirus Cancer Vaccines Show Robust Immunity and Safety but Modest
news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 21, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Adenovirus Cancer Vaccines Show Robust Immunity and Safety but Modest Single-Agent Efficacy by November 20, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 8 mins read 0 Adenovirus Cancer Vaccines Show Robust Immunity and Safety but Modest Single-Agent Efficacy Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive systematic review evaluating clinical trials of adenovirus-based cancer vaccines reveals that these platforms reliably trigger targeted cellular immune responses and maintain a predominantly mild safety profile, although their ability to shrink tumors as standalone treatments remains constrained. Published in the journal Infectious Agents and Cancer, the investigation systematically examined clinical evidence collected across human oncology trials published through February 2026. The authors synthesized findings from twenty clinical trials conducted between 2000 and 2025 to determine how recombinant adenoviral vectors perform regarding participant safety, biological immunogenicity, and objective therapeutic outcomes. The analysis demonstrated that while these viral platforms consistently succeed in stimulating antigen-specific cytotoxic CD8-positive and helper CD4-positive T-cell responses across multiple tumor types, translating these biological reactions into objective tumor regression represents an ongoing hurdle. In the majority of monotherapy evaluations, clinical benefit manifested primarily as disease stabilization and prolonged disease control rather than dramatic objective response rates, highlighting a therapeutic disparity shaped by pre-existing anti-vector neutralizing immunity and suppressive mechanisms within the tumor microenvironment. The study protocol was established following methodological standards outlined by the Cochrane Collaboration Handbook and adhered strictly to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Before study execution, the review protocol was formally registered in August 2025 within the international prospective register of systematic reviews, PROSPERO, under registration identifier CRD420251079521. Investigators conducted literature searches across PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by targeted queries in ClinicalTrials.gov and Google Scholar. The search strategy combined controlled Medical Subject Headings and text keywords relating to adenoviruses, viral vaccines, neoplasms, and immunotherapy, capturing records up to an initial cutoff of May 2025 and subsequently updated through February 2026. After removing duplicate entries using bibliographic software, two independent reviewers evaluated 604 unique titles and abstracts. A total of 573 records were excluded for falling outside predefined eligibility criteria, which specifically eliminated preclinical animal models, in vitro laboratory experiments, non-adenoviral viral vector systems, non-oncology applications, case reports, review articles, and studies without accessible full texts. Ultimately, thirty-one full-text reports were assessed in detail, yielding twenty completed clinical trials that satisfied all methodological inclusion criteria. The included trials investigated therapeutic adenoviral interventions across diverse patient populations suffering from solid malignancies, predominantly in advanced disease stages where standard therapeutic interventions had failed or recurrence had occurred. Across the twenty trials, fifteen were categorized as Phase I dose-escalation evaluations, three were conducted as Phase I/II investigations, and one was executed as a Phase II trial. Malignancies targeted within the cohort reflected prevalent solid tumors, led by colorectal cancer in seven trials, prostate cancer in six trials, lung cancer in six trials, breast cancer in three trials, and cutaneous melanoma in two trials, along with focused evaluations in cervical and hepatocellular carcinomas. To deliver targeted genetic material, investigators relied heavily on human serotype 5 adenoviral vectors, which were utilized in ten clinical studies. Six investigations implemented chimpanzee-derived adenoviral vectors to circumvent the widespread prevalence of human neutralizing antibodies, while minor subsets utilized human serotype 6 in two trials and serotype 2 in two trials. The vector constructs carried a diverse array of tumor-associated antigens and neoantigens, including prostate-specific antigen, carcinoembryonic antigen, mucin 1, HER2, prostate-specific membrane antigen, and brachyury, as well as specialized targets such as alpha-fetoprotein, GUCY2C, human telomerase reverse transcriptase, HPV oncogenes E5, E6, and E7, and mutated KRAS and TP53. Discover more cancer vaccines Cancer Vaccines Find Cancer Care vaccines vaccine Administration protocols varied across the reviewed literature, reflecting the versatility of adenoviral delivery vehicles. Intramuscular injection served as the most frequent route of administration, appearing in twelve trials, followed by subcutaneous delivery in eight trials and intradermal injection in one study. Dosing regimens typically ranged from 10 to the power of 7 up to 10 to the power of 12 viral particles per immunization. Regarding treatment architecture, seven studies evaluated adenovirus-based vaccines as pure monotherapies, while the remaining thirteen investigated multifaceted combination regimens. Seven trials incorporated prime-boost schedules using plasmid DNA vaccines as either priming or boosting agents alongside adenoviral vectors to broaden and sustain the cellular immune response. Two studies coupled adenoviral vectors with Modified Vaccinia Ankara vector vaccines, and four trials combined adenoviral immunization with immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1 or PD-L1 signaling pathways. Across all included investigations, treatment-related safety and patient tolerability served as primary clinical endpoints, while secondary outcomes systematically measured antigen-specific cellular immunogenicity, progression-free survival, overall survival, and tumor response classified according to standard RECIST criteria. Safety analyses documented across all twenty trials established that adenoviral cancer vaccines generally demonstrate an acceptable and manageable safety profile. Across eighteen trials that provided granular adverse event data, the overwhelming majority of treatment-related toxicities were classified as mild to moderate Grade 1 or Grade 2 events that were transient and resolved spontaneously within twenty-four hours post-immunization. Local injection-site reactions constituted the most frequent adverse effect, documented across fourteen clinical studies with study-specific incidence rates ranging from 11 percent to 94.4 percent. These local manifestations routinely consisted of temporary localized erythema, tenderness, swelling, and discomfort. Systemic adverse reactions were similarly consistent with expected physiological responses to viral vector immunization and innate immune stimulation. Systemic fatigue emerged as the most widespread constitutional symptom, identified in fifteen trials with frequencies between 5 percent and 72 percent. Additional recurring Grade 1 and 2 reactions included pyrexia or fever ranging from 10 percent to 86 percent, influenza-like illness spanning 17 percent to 60 percent, rigors or chills reported in 16 percent to 80 percent, and myalgia documented between 10 percent and 70 percent. Gastrointestinal and neurological disturbances such as nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, headaches, and transient dizziness occurred at modest frequencies across the investigated cohorts. Severe treatment-related adverse events meeting Grade 3 or higher criteria were distinctly uncommon across the clinical trial database, with only two studies documenting life-threatening complications or fatal toxicities linked to treatment administration. In one trial conducted by Diaz and colleagues, two enrolled patients experienced Grade 3 adverse events involving localized muscle spasms and unilateral leg pain; however, both occurrences were clinically assessed as unrelated to the vaccine vector, and no dose-limiting toxicities or long-term serious events emerged during one-year follow-up monitoring. In a separate trial evaluating the PRGN-2009 adenoviral vaccine administered concurrently with the bifunctional fusion protein bintrafusp alfa, Grade 3 and 4 events comprising duodenal hemorrhage in two patients and severe throat mucositis in one patient necessitated hospital admission. Both individuals presenting with duodenal bleeding were concurrently taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and one patient subsequently died after refusing corrective blood transfusions on religious grounds, a fatality not attributed directly to the viral vaccine. The sole trial to systematically report higher-grade treatment-related toxicities directly attributable to vector-based intervention was conducted by Autio and coworkers. In that trial, 41.1 percent of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and 60 percent of patients in a biochemical recurrence cohort developed Grade 3 or 4 adverse events. Furthermore, two fatal Grade 5 toxicities occurred among ninety treated participants: one patient experienced a fatal pulmonary embolism secondary to treatment-associated myasthenia gravis, while a second participant succumbed to severe immune-mediated myocarditis, yielding a treatment-related mortality rate of 2.2 percent within that specific study population. The occurrence of immune-mediated myocarditis observed in clinical testing mirrors documented, albeit rare, cardiovascular safety signals detected during the global rollout of adenoviral-vectored COVID-19 vaccines, such as ChAdOx1 and Ad26.COV2.S. In the systematic review, the authors noted that while vaccine-associated myocarditis was historically more pronounced following mRNA-based vaccines administered to young male recipients, viral vectors share overlapping immunological mechanisms of innate immune stimulation. The biological mechanisms proposed for these cardiovascular events involve intense activation of pattern recognition receptors, including Toll-like receptor 9 and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase stimulator of interferon genes pathways, which trigger elevated releases of type I interferons and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Additionally, potential molecular mimicry between vector-encoded viral structures or expressional antigens and host myocardial tissue may contribute to tissue inflammation in susceptible individuals. Because adenoviral cancer platforms intentionally harness vigorous innate immune adjuvanticity to initiate adaptive antitumor immunity, the researchers stressed that future oncology clinical trials must integrate proactive cardiac surveillance protocols, including baseline and post-vaccination electrocardiograms and serum cardiac troponin measurements, particularly in patient cohorts with pre-existing cardiovascular risk factors. Assessment of secondary immunological outcomes demonstrated that adenoviral vectors excel at provoking targeted adaptive cellular immunity. All twenty included trials monitored cellular immunogenicity using validated laboratory techniques, including enzyme-linked immunospot assays measuring interferon-gamma secretion, delayed-type hypersensitivity skin reactions, and multi-parameter flow cytometry. Eighteen of the twenty clinical trials verified that vaccination successfully expanded circulating pools of functional CD8-positive cytotoxic T lymphocytes and CD4-positive helper T cells specifically reactive against target tumor antigens. Detectable immune activation was observed against widespread tumor antigens including carcinoembryonic antigen, prostate-specific antigen, MUC-1, HER2, brachyury, and alpha-fetoprotein following one or more immunizations. Only two trials failed to detect measurable cellular immune responses against intended tumor antigens. In the study by Diaz and coworkers evaluating prime-boost regimens for HER2 and carcinoembryonic antigen, patients developed robust immune responses against an incorporated bacterial enterotoxin component, demonstrating effective vector delivery and dendritic cell presentation, yet failed to mount cellular responses against the targeted tumor antigens due to their weak inherent immunogenicity in a heterogeneous patient population. Similarly, an investigation by Nemunaitis and colleagues evaluating an Ad5 vector expressing L523S observed an absence of measurable antigen-specific T-cell activation, leading those investigators to suggest combination approaches to enhance cellular reactivity. Despite widespread and consistent biological immunogenicity, objective clinical antitumor efficacy remained modest across the included trials, particularly when adenovirus-based vaccines were administered as monotherapies. Objective response rates measuring substantial radiographic tumor shrinkage remained low in early-phase cohorts. Instead, the predominant clinical manifestation of therapeutic activity was disease stabilization. For example, one reviewed clinical study observed that while the confirmed objective response rate was zero percent, 77.8 percent of enrolled patients achieved sustained stable disease. Across the literature, six studies formally reported stable disease, five noted partial responses, three observed complete responses, four reported progressive disease, and three recorded objective response metrics. In cohorts reporting survival metrics, median progression-free survival reached 22 weeks in one study of patients with advanced malignancies. The systematic review highlighted that the presence of circulating, antigen-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes does not guarantee effective infiltration into immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Consequently, traditional objective response rate assessments may underestimate the clinical utility of cancer vaccines, underscoring progression-free survival and duration of stable disease as more relevant clinical endpoints for measuring biological tumor control. Methodological quality appraisal conducted with the Cochrane Collaboration risk of bias tool revealed substantial structural limitations within the published evidence base. Nineteen of the twenty included clinical trials were judged to possess an overall high risk of bias, while only one trial, a randomized Phase I evaluation conducted by Cappuccini and colleagues in 2020, received a moderate risk rating. The high risk of bias across eighteen trials stemmed directly from their non-randomized, open-label, dose-escalation Phase I trial designs, which inherently lack random sequence generation, allocation concealment, and participant or personnel blinding. Conversely, blinding of outcome assessors for laboratory-based immunological assays was rated as low risk in half of the included trials due to the use of objective automated assay instrumentation. Incomplete outcome reporting and selective reporting domains were broadly classified as low risk because early-phase clinical protocols comprehensively disclosed safety and immunogenicity findings for all enrolled participants. The authors noted that this prevalent high risk of bias reflects necessary early-stage trial architectures rather than poor methodological execution, but cautioned that the absence of large-scale randomized controlled trials restricts data synthesis, meta-analytic pooling, and broad generalizability. Looking toward future clinical translation, the systematic review identified thirteen active and ongoing clinical trials investigating adenovirus-based cancer vaccines, consisting of seven Phase II trials, five Phase I/II investigations, and one Phase IV study. These ongoing efforts reflect a strategic transition away from unselected monotherapy regimens and toward rational combination paradigms. By combining adenoviral platforms with immune checkpoint inhibitors, radiation therapy, or chemotherapy, clinicians aim to counteract tumor immune evasion, reverse local immunosuppression, and allow vaccine-induced cytotoxic T cells to penetrate solid tumors effectively. Furthermore, modern vector engineering approaches, such as the adoption of non-human adenoviral serotypes like chimpanzee adenoviruses, directly address the challenge of pre-existing neutralizing antibodies that can prematurely clear viral particles before optimal dendritic cell transduction occurs. The review concluded that while early clinical evidence definitively validates the safety and immunogenicity of adenoviral cancer vaccines, definitive proof of clinical efficacy will require well-powered, randomized clinical trials evaluating optimized vectors and targeted combination strategies in defined patient populations. Published in the journal Infectious Agents and Cancer, the investigation systematically examined clinical evidence collected across human oncology trials published through February 2026. The authors synthesized findings from twenty clinical trials conducted between 2000 and 2025 to determine how recombinant adenoviral vectors perform regarding participant safety, biological immunogenicity, and objective therapeutic outcomes. The analysis demonstrated that while these viral platforms consistently succeed in stimulating antigen-specific cytotoxic CD8-positive and helper CD4-positive T-cell responses across multiple tumor types, translating these biological reactions into objective tumor regression represents an ongoing hurdle. In the majority of monotherapy evaluations, clinical benefit manifested primarily as disease stabilization and prolonged disease control rather than dramatic objective response rates, highlighting a therapeutic disparity shaped by pre-existing anti-vector neutralizing immunity and suppressive mechanisms within the tumor microenvironment. The study protocol was established following methodological standards outlined by the Cochrane Collaboration Handbook and adhered strictly to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Before study execution, the review protocol was formally registered in August 2025 within the international prospective register of systematic reviews, PROSPERO, under registration identifier CRD420251079521. Investigators conducted literature searches across PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by targeted queries in ClinicalTrials.gov and Google Scholar. The search strategy combined controlled Medical Subject Headings and text keywords relating to adenoviruses, viral vaccines, neoplasms, and immunotherapy, capturing records up to an initial cutoff of May 2025 and subsequently updated through February 2026. After removing duplicate entries using bibliographic software, two independent reviewers evaluated 604 unique titles and abstracts. A total of 573 records were excluded for falling outside predefined eligibility criteria, which specifically eliminated preclinical animal models, in vitro laboratory experiments, non-adenoviral viral vector systems, non-oncology applications, case reports, review articles, and studies without accessible full texts. Ultimately, thirty-one full-text reports were assessed in detail, yielding twenty completed clinical trials that satisfied all methodological inclusion criteria. The included trials investigated therapeutic adenoviral interventions across diverse patient populations suffering from solid malignancies, predominantly in advanced disease stages where standard therapeutic interventions had failed or recurrence had occurred. Across the twenty trials, fifteen were categorized as Phase I dose-escalation evaluations, three were conducted as Phase I/II investigations, and one was executed as a Phase II trial. Malignancies targeted within the cohort reflected prevalent solid tumors, led by colorectal cancer in seven trials, prostate cancer in six trials, lung cancer in six trials, breast cancer in three trials, and cutaneous melanoma in two trials, along with focused evaluations in cervical and hepatocellular carcinomas. To deliver targeted genetic material, investigators relied heavily on human serotype 5 adenoviral vectors, which were utilized in ten clinical studies. Six investigations implemented chimpanzee-derived adenoviral vectors to circumvent the widespread prevalence of human neutralizing antibodies, while minor subsets utilized human serotype 6 in two trials and serotype 2 in two trials. The vector constructs carried a diverse array of tumor-associated antigens and neoantigens, including prostate-specific antigen, carcinoembryonic antigen, mucin 1, HER2, prostate-specific membrane antigen, and brachyury, as well as specialized targets such as alpha-fetoprotein, GUCY2C, human telomerase reverse transcriptase, HPV oncogenes E5, E6, and E7, and mutated KRAS and TP53. Discover more cancer vaccines Cancer Vaccines Find Cancer Care vaccines vaccine Administration protocols varied across the reviewed literature, reflecting the versatility of adenoviral delivery vehicles. Intramuscular injection served as the most frequent route of administration, appearing in twelve trials, followed by subcutaneous delivery in eight trials and intradermal injection in one study. Dosing regimens typically ranged from 10 to the power of 7 up to 10 to the power of 12 viral particles per immunization. Regarding treatment architecture, seven studies evaluated adenovirus-based vaccines as pure monotherapies, while the remaining thirteen investigated multifaceted combination regimens. Seven trials incorporated prime-boost schedules using plasmid DNA vaccines as either priming or boosting agents alongside adenoviral vectors to broaden and sustain the cellular immune response. Two studies coupled adenoviral vectors with Modified Vaccinia Ankara vector vaccines, and four trials combined adenoviral immunization with immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1 or PD-L1 signaling pathways. Across all included investigations, treatment-related safety and patient tolerability served as primary clinical endpoints, while secondary outcomes systematically measured antigen-specific cellular immunogenicity, progression-free survival, overall survival, and tumor response classified according to standard RECIST criteria. Safety analyses documented across all twenty trials established that adenoviral cancer vaccines generally demonstrate an acceptable and manageable safety profile. Across eighteen trials that provided granular adverse event data, the overwhelming majority of treatment-related toxicities were classified as mild to moderate Grade 1 or Grade 2 events that were transient and resolved spontaneously within twenty-four hours post-immunization. Local injection-site reactions constituted the most frequent adverse effect, documented across fourteen clinical studies with study-specific incidence rates ranging from 11 percent to 94.4 percent. These local manifestations routinely consisted of temporary localized erythema, tenderness, swelling, and discomfort. Systemic adverse reactions were similarly consistent with expected physiological responses to viral vector immunization and innate immune stimulation. Systemic fatigue emerged as the most widespread constitutional symptom, identified in fifteen trials with frequencies between 5 percent and 72 percent. Additional recurring Grade 1 and 2 reactions included pyrexia or fever ranging from 10 percent to 86 percent, influenza-like illness spanning 17 percent to 60 percent, rigors or chills reported in 16 percent to 80 percent, and myalgia documented between 10 percent and 70 percent. Gastrointestinal and neurological disturbances such as nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, headaches, and transient dizziness occurred at modest frequencies across the investigated cohorts. Severe treatment-related adverse events meeting Grade 3 or higher criteria were distinctly uncommon across the clinical trial database, with only two studies documenting life-threatening complications or fatal toxicities linked to treatment administration. In one trial conducted by Diaz and colleagues, two enrolled patients experienced Grade 3 adverse events involving localized muscle spasms and unilateral leg pain; however, both occurrences were clinically assessed as unrelated to the vaccine vector, and no dose-limiting toxicities or long-term serious events emerged during one-year follow-up monitoring. In a separate trial evaluating the PRGN-2009 adenoviral vaccine administered concurrently with the bifunctional fusion protein bintrafusp alfa, Grade 3 and 4 events comprising duodenal hemorrhage in two patients and severe throat mucositis in one patient necessitated hospital admission. Both individuals presenting with duodenal bleeding were concurrently taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and one patient subsequently died after refusing corrective blood transfusions on religious grounds, a fatality not attributed directly to the viral vaccine. The sole trial to systematically report higher-grade treatment-related toxicities directly attributable to vector-based intervention was conducted by Autio and coworkers. In that trial, 41.1 percent of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and 60 percent of patients in a biochemical recurrence cohort developed Grade 3 or 4 adverse events. Furthermore, two fatal Grade 5 toxicities occurred among ninety treated participants: one patient experienced a fatal pulmonary embolism secondary to treatment-associated myasthenia gravis, while a second participant succumbed to severe immune-mediated myocarditis, yielding a treatment-related mortality rate of 2.2 percent within that specific study population. The occurrence of immune-mediated myocarditis observed in clinical testing mirrors documented, albeit rare, cardiovascular safety signals detected during the global rollout of adenoviral-vectored COVID-19 vaccines, such as ChAdOx1 and Ad26.COV2.S. In the systematic review, the authors noted that while vaccine-associated myocarditis was historically more pronounced following mRNA-based vaccines administered to young male recipients, viral vectors share overlapping immunological mechanisms of innate immune stimulation. The biological mechanisms proposed for these cardiovascular events involve intense activation of pattern recognition receptors, including Toll-like receptor 9 and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase stimulator of interferon genes pathways, which trigger elevated releases of type I interferons and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Additionally, potential molecular mimicry between vector-encoded viral structures or expressional antigens and host myocardial tissue may contribute to tissue inflammation in susceptible individuals. Because adenoviral cancer platforms intentionally harness vigorous innate immune adjuvanticity to initiate adaptive antitumor immunity, the researchers stressed that future oncology clinical trials must integrate proactive cardiac surveillance protocols, including baseline and post-vaccination electrocardiograms and serum cardiac troponin measurements, particularly in patient cohorts with pre-existing cardiovascular risk factors. Assessment of secondary immunological outcomes demonstrated that adenoviral vectors excel at provoking targeted adaptive cellular immunity. All twenty included trials monitored cellular immunogenicity using validated laboratory techniques, including enzyme-linked immunospot assays measuring interferon-gamma secretion, delayed-type hypersensitivity skin reactions, and multi-parameter flow cytometry. Eighteen of the twenty clinical trials verified that vaccination successfully expanded circulating pools of functional CD8-positive cytotoxic T lymphocytes and CD4-positive helper T cells specifically reactive against target tumor antigens. Detectable immune activation was observed against widespread tumor antigens including carcinoembryonic antigen, prostate-specific antigen, MUC-1, HER2, brachyury, and alpha-fetoprotein following one or more immunizations. Only two trials failed to detect measurable cellular immune responses against intended tumor antigens. In the study by Diaz and coworkers evaluating prime-boost regimens for HER2 and carcinoembryonic antigen, patients developed robust immune responses against an incorporated bacterial enterotoxin component, demonstrating effective vector delivery and dendritic cell presentation, yet failed to mount cellular responses against the targeted tumor antigens due to their weak inherent immunogenicity in a heterogeneous patient population. Similarly, an investigation by Nemunaitis and colleagues evaluating an Ad5 vector expressing L523S observed an absence of measurable antigen-specific T-cell activation, leading those investigators to suggest combination approaches to enhance cellular reactivity. Despite widespread and consistent biological immunogenicity, objective clinical antitumor efficacy remained modest across the included trials, particularly when adenovirus-based vaccines were administered as monotherapies. Objective response rates measuring substantial radiographic tumor shrinkage remained low in early-phase cohorts. Instead, the predominant clinical manifestation of therapeutic activity was disease stabilization. For example, one reviewed clinical study observed that while the confirmed objective response rate was zero percent, 77.8 percent of enrolled patients achieved sustained stable disease. Across the literature, six studies formally reported stable disease, five noted partial responses, three observed complete responses, four reported progressive disease, and three recorded objective response metrics. In cohorts reporting survival metrics, median progression-free survival reached 22 weeks in one study of patients with advanced malignancies. The systematic review highlighted that the presence of circulating, antigen-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes does not guarantee effective infiltration into immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Consequently, traditional objective response rate assessments may underestimate the clinical utility of cancer vaccines, underscoring progression-free survival and duration of stable disease as more relevant clinical endpoints for measuring biological tumor control. Methodological quality appraisal conducted with the Cochrane Collaboration risk of bias tool revealed substantial structural limitations within the published evidence base. Nineteen of the twenty included clinical trials were judged to possess an overall high risk of bias, while only one trial, a randomized Phase I evaluation conducted by Cappuccini and colleagues in 2020, received a moderate risk rating. The high risk of bias across eighteen trials stemmed directly from their non-randomized, open-label, dose-escalation Phase I trial designs, which inherently lack random sequence generation, allocation concealment, and participant or personnel blinding. Conversely, blinding of outcome assessors for laboratory-based immunological assays was rated as low risk in half of the included trials due to the use of objective automated assay instrumentation. Incomplete outcome reporting and selective reporting domains were broadly classified as low risk because early-phase clinical protocols comprehensively disclosed safety and immunogenicity findings for all enrolled participants. The authors noted that this prevalent high risk of bias reflects necessary early-stage trial architectures rather than poor methodological execution, but cautioned that the absence of large-scale randomized controlled trials restricts data synthesis, meta-analytic pooling, and broad generalizability. Looking toward future clinical translation, the systematic review identified thirteen active and ongoing clinical trials investigating adenovirus-based cancer vaccines, consisting of seven Phase II trials, five Phase I/II investigations, and one Phase IV study. These ongoing efforts reflect a strategic transition away from unselected monotherapy regimens and toward rational combination paradigms. By combining adenoviral platforms with immune checkpoint inhibitors, radiation therapy, or chemotherapy, clinicians aim to counteract tumor immune evasion, reverse local immunosuppression, and allow vaccine-induced cytotoxic T cells to penetrate solid tumors effectively. Furthermore, modern vector engineering approaches, such as the adoption of non-human adenoviral serotypes like chimpanzee adenoviruses, directly address the challenge of pre-existing neutralizing antibodies that can prematurely clear viral particles before optimal dendritic cell transduction occurs. The review concluded that while early clinical evidence definitively validates the safety and immunogenicity of adenoviral cancer vaccines, definitive proof of clinical efficacy will require well-powered, randomized clinical trials evaluating optimized vectors and targeted combination strategies in defined patient populations. However, the study found that their single-agent efficacy in shrinking tumors remains modest. The analysis included twenty clinical trials conducted between 2000 and 2025, targeting various solid malignancies such as colorectal, prostate, lung, breast, and cutaneous melanoma. The majority of trials showed disease stabilization and prolonged control rather than significant tumor regression. Adverse events were generally mild to moderate, with no direct fatalities attributed to the vaccines. The study followed Cochrane Collaboration and PRISMA guidelines, with thirty-one full-text reports assessed and twenty trials meeting inclusion criteria. news.content_zh: Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 11 月 20 日发表的系统评价评估了基于腺病毒的癌症 疫苗,强调了它们触发强大的细胞 免疫应答 并保持温和安全性的能力。然而,研究发现它们在缩小肿瘤方面的单药疗效仍然有限。该分析包括 2000 年至 2025 年间进行的 20 项临床试验,针对各种实体恶性肿瘤,如结直肠癌、前列腺癌、肺癌、乳腺癌和皮肤黑色素瘤。大多数试验显示疾病稳定和长期控制,而不是显着的肿瘤消退。不良事件一般为轻度至中度,疫苗 没有造成直接死亡。该研究遵循 Cochrane Collaboration 和 PRISMA 指南,评估了 31 份全文报告,20 项试验符合纳入标准。研究结果基于对临床证据的全面分析,并将结果作为系统评价的一部分进行报告。
